en: Thus have I heard: [Majjhima Nikāya 17, Vanapatthasutta]
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!”
“Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Bhikkhus, I will teach you the discourse on forest retreats.”
“Listen to that and attend closely; I shall speak.
“Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Here, monks, a monk dwells in dependence upon a certain forest grove.
While he is dwelling in dependence upon that forest grove, his unestablished mindfulness does not become established;
his unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated; his undestroyed taints do not go to destruction; and what has not yet been attained—”
He does not attain the unsurpassed security from bondage.
Furthermore, those requisites of life that must be procured by one who has gone forth—namely, robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for use in sickness—are obtained with difficulty.
Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should reflect thus:
‘I am indeed living in dependence upon this forest retreat; yet for me, while living in dependence upon this forest retreat,
mindfulness that has not been established does not become established, the unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated,
the unabated taints do not go to their destruction, and the unsurpassed security from bondage that has not been attained is not reached.’
‘And these requisites for the life of one gone forth that must be procured—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for use in sickness—are obtained with difficulty.
In such a case, monks, that monk should depart from that forest thicket during either the night or the day;
he should not remain there. But here, monks, a monk dwells in dependence upon a certain forest thicket.
While he dwells in dependence on that forest retreat, his unestablished mindfulness does not become established;
his unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated; his unabandoned taints do not reach their exhaustion;
and he does not attain the unsurpassed security from bondage that has not yet been attained.

And whatever requisites for life are to be procured by one who has gone forth—the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal supplies as support for the sick—these are obtained without difficulty.
Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should reflect thus:
“I am living in dependence on this forest thicket. For me, in dependence on this forest thicket...”
While dwelling thus, mindfulness that has not yet been established does not become established; the unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated;
the taints that have not yet been exhausted do not go to their exhaustion; and the unsurpassed security from bondage that has not yet been reached is not attained.
Yet those requisites of life that must be procured by one gone forth—the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal supports for the sick—are obtained without difficulty.

Indeed, it was not for the sake of robes that I went forth from the home life into homelessness, nor for the sake of almsfood... nor for the sake of lodgings... nor for the sake of medicinal requisites for the sick that I went forth from the home life into homelessness.

And yet, as I dwell depending on this forest thicket, my unestablished mindfulness does not become established, my unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, and my unabandoned taints do not reach their exhaustion.
‘I have not attained, nor am I reaching, the unsurpassed security from bondage,’ then, monks, that monk should depart from that forest retreat;
he should not remain there. But here, monks, a monk dwells in dependence on a certain forest retreat.
For him dwelling in dependence on that forest retreat, mindfulness that had not yet been established becomes established;
his unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated; his unabated taints reach their exhaustion; and he attains the unsurpassed security from bondage that he had not yet attained.
"But those requisites of life that must be procured by one who has gone forth—namely, robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick—are obtained with difficulty.
Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should reflect thus:
'I am living in dependence upon this forest thicket.'"
As I dwell depending on this forest retreat, my unestablished mindfulness becomes established,
my unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, my unabandoned taints go to their destruction, and I attain the unsurpassed security from bondage that I had not yet attained.
Furthermore, these requisites of life that must be procured by one who has gone forth—namely, robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick—are obtained with difficulty.
Yet, I did not go forth from the home life into homelessness for the sake of robes, nor for the sake of almsfood, nor for the sake of lodgings, nor for the sake of medicinal requisites for the sick.
Nevertheless, as I dwell here in dependence on this forest thicket, my unestablished mindfulness becomes established.
‘My unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, my unabandoned taints go to their destruction, and I attain the unsurpassed security from bondage that has not yet been attained.
For this reason, monks, that monk should stay even for a countable period in that forest retreat; he should not depart.
But here, monks, a monk dwells in dependence upon a certain forest thicket.
For him dwelling in dependence upon that forest thicket, mindfulness that was unestablished becomes established;
his unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated; his unabandoned taints go to their destruction; and the unsurpassed... [that he had not yet attained]... is attained.
He attains the security from bondage.
And those requisites of life that must be procured by one who has gone forth—namely, robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for use in sickness—are obtained without difficulty.
Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should reflect thus:
‘I am indeed dwelling in dependence upon this forest retreat. While I am dwelling here in dependence upon this forest retreat,
my unestablished mindfulness becomes established, my unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated,
my unabandoned taints go to their destruction, and I attain the unsurpassed security from bondage that I had not yet attained.’
‘And these requisites for life that must be procured by one who has gone forth—the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained without difficulty.
In that case, monks, that monk should dwell in that forest grove for as long as he lives; he should not depart.
Here, monks, a monk dwells in dependence on a certain village... [as before]...
He dwells in dependence on a certain market town …pe… he dwells in dependence on a certain city …pe… he dwells in dependence on a certain district …pe…
He dwells depending upon a certain person.
While he is dwelling depending upon that person, his unestablished mindfulness does not become established,
his unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, his unabandoned taints do not go to their destruction, and what has not yet been attained...
He does not attain the unsurpassed security from bondage.
Furthermore, those requisites of life that must be procured by one who has gone forth—the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained with difficulty.
Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should reflect thus:
‘I am indeed living in dependence upon this person.
While I am living in dependence upon this person, my unestablished mindfulness does not become established; my unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated;
my unabandoned taints do not go to their destruction; and I do not attain the unsurpassed security from bondage that has not yet been attained.’
‘And these requisites for life that must be procured by one who has gone forth—the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained with difficulty.
In such a case, monks, that bhikkhu should depart from that person either during the night or during the day without taking leave, and he should not follow after him.
Furthermore, monks, there is the case where a bhikkhu dwells in dependence upon a certain person.
For one who dwells in dependence upon that person, mindfulness that has not yet been established does not become established;
the unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated; the taints that have not yet been exhausted do not go to their exhaustion;
and the unsurpassed security from bondage that has not yet been attained is not reached.
"And those requisites of life that must be procured by one who has gone forth—the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained without difficulty.
Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should reflect thus:
'I am living in dependence upon this person. While I am living in dependence upon this person...'"
My unestablished mindfulness does not become established; my unconcentrated mind does not attain concentration;
my unabandoned taints do not go to their destruction; and I do not reach the unsurpassed security from bondage that has not yet been reached.
Yet, those requisites of life that must be procured by one gone forth—the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained without difficulty.

"Yet it was not for the sake of robes that I went forth from the home life into homelessness; nor for the sake of almsfood... nor for the sake of lodgings... nor for the sake of medicinal requisites for the sick did I go forth from the home life into homelessness.

And yet, while dwelling in dependence upon this person, my unestablished mindfulness does not become established, my unconcentrated mind does not become concentrated, and my unabandoned taints do not reach their exhaustion."
‘I am not attaining the unsurpassed security from bondage that has not yet been attained.
In such a case, monks, even if that person has given leave, that monk should depart and should not follow after him.
But here, monks, a monk dwells in dependence upon a certain person.
For one who dwells in dependence upon that person, mindfulness that was not yet established becomes established;
the unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated; the taints that were not yet exhausted reach exhaustion; and the unsurpassed security from bondage that had not yet been attained is fully reached.
But those requisites for life that must be procured by one who has gone forth—the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal supplies for the sick—are obtained with difficulty.
Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should reflect thus:
"I am living in dependence upon this person. While I am living in dependence upon this person..."
Unestablished mindfulness becomes established; the unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated;
the unabandoned taints go to their destruction; and I attain the unsurpassed security from bondage that has not yet been attained.
Furthermore, those requisites of life that must be procured by one gone forth—namely, robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick—are obtained with difficulty.

"Yet it was not for the sake of robes that I went forth from the home life into homelessness; nor for the sake of almsfood... nor for the sake of lodgings... nor for the sake of medicinal requisites for use in sickness did I go forth from the home life into homelessness.

Rather, while dwelling in dependence upon this person, my unestablished mindfulness becomes established, my unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated, and my unabandoned taints go to their destruction; and what has not yet been attained..."
‘I shall attain the unsurpassed security from bondage.
In that case, monks, that monk should follow after that person even for the sake of calculation; he should not depart.
But here, monks, a monk dwells in dependence upon a certain person.
For one who dwells in dependence upon that person, mindfulness that had not yet been established becomes established;

the unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated; the untainted taints that were not yet exhausted reach exhaustion; and the unsurpassed security from bondage that had not yet been attained is fully reached.

"And those requisites for the livelihood of one who has gone forth—namely, robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick—that are to be procured, these come to him without difficulty.
Therefore, monks, that bhikkhu should reflect thus:
'I am living in dependence upon this person. While I am living in dependence upon this person, [the requisites... "
‘Unestablished mindfulness becomes established; the unconcentrated mind becomes concentrated;
the unabandoned taints go to their destruction; and I attain the unsurpassed security from bondage not yet attained.
Furthermore, those requisites of life that must be procured by one gone forth—namely, robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick—are obtained without difficulty.’”
"Therefore, monks, that monk should follow after that person for as long as life lasts; he must not depart, even if he is being driven away.
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
The monks, glad at heart, rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The Vanapatthasutta, the seventh, is finished.
